chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ، عَنِ الْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ، عَنِ الْأَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ، عَنِ الزُّرَارَةِ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامِ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from al-Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

chunks.arabic_text: أَنَّ الْمَهْدِيَّ مَوْلَى عُثْمَانَ أَتَى فَبَايَعَ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ جَالِسٌ، قَالَ: أَبَايِعُكَ عَلَى أَنَّ الْأَمْرَ كَانَ لَكَ أَوَّلًا وَ أَبْرَأُ مِنْ فُلَانٍ وَ فُلَانٍ وَ فُلَانٍ، فَبَايَعَهُ

translations.en: That al-Mahdi, the client of Uthman, came and pledged allegiance to the Commander of the Faithful, while Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr was seated. He said: I pledge allegiance to you on the condition that the matter [of leadership] was yours from the beginning, and I disassociate myself from so-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so, so he pledged allegiance to him.

en.summary: This narration from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights the political legitimacy of Imam Ali (AS) through the testimony of al-Mahdi, identified here as the client (mawla) of Uthman, who publicly affirmed that the imamate was Ali's right from the outset. His pledge, accompanied by disassociation (bara'ah) from specific rivals, underscores the early recognition of Ali's authority even among those connected to the preceding caliphs, a key theme in Shia historiography regarding the succession after the Prophet.
en.seo_question: Who did al-Mahdi pledge allegiance to and what was his declaration regarding the caliphate?

key_terms.الْمَهْدِي: Al-Mahdi (the guided one), here referring to a specific companion/client of Uthman
key_terms.مَوْلَى: Client or freedman, indicating a social relationship
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.الْأَمْر: The matter, referring to leadership or caliphate
